quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane provide for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane has three paths for motorcyclists: the left side, the center, and the right side of the lane.

questions.question: When following a car, what is the best part of the lane to ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when following a car. This way, the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers look at their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without making the new rider lead the group.

questions.question: What is the best group formation when riding through curves, turning, or entering a highway?
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when traveling normally, but switch to single-file when riding through curves, making turns, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled bikes. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of a curve to stay safe.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket while riding in warm weather?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take breaks to cool off.
Yes, riding jackets keep you cool in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets keep you cool in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket in warm weather. Jackets protect you and help prevent dehydration. Many jackets are designed to keep riders cool even in hot weather.

questions.question: Which statement is true about motorcycle brakes?

options.text: The front and rear brakes have equal stopping power.
The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
The rear brake is stronger than the front brake.
Use only the front brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake provides more stopping power than the rear brake—at least 70 percent of total stopping power. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: Helmeted riders are how many times more likely to survive a crash than riders without helmets?
questions.explanation: At any speed, wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive head injuries in a crash compared to not wearing one.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to see where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes to reduce your reaction time. This is especially helpful when riding through areas where hazards may appear.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Press the front brake hard to stop the front tire from locking.
Use one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the front brake gently to avoid locking the front wheel. Use light pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: Proper riding clothes provide all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you from crashes and bad weather. Good clothes should provide comfort, not discomfort.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than normal.
Stay farther back from the car ahead.
Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: With a passenger, your motorcycle is heavier and slower to respond. Ride slower, start stopping sooner, and increase your distance from other cars. Always talk to your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden moves, and use both brakes gently. Never brake hard and fast.

questions.question: If your front wheel starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Keep pressing the front brake and ride it out.
Keep pressing the front brake and release the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then press it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then press it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks up, release the front brake completely and immediately. Then apply it again gently.

questions.question: What is the best formation when riding in a group?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to a single line when turning, going around curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride right behind the leader. This way they don't fall behind, and experienced riders can watch them.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
It depends on the riding conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the riding conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Choose a position based on your current conditions. Stay far enough from other vehicles and make sure others can see you.

questions.question: A small animal enters your lane in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Swerve into another lane to avoid it, no matter what.
Switch lanes as fast as possible.
Flash your lights to scare it away.

questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal if it is safe. In traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving could cause you to hit another vehicle. A small animal is less dangerous than a crash.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is not recommended because it can cause heat-related illness.
Should only be worn if the jacket is light colored.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: You should wear a riding jacket and long pants even in hot weather. They protect you from injuries and also help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are used for road rules like speed limits. They are white with black lettering or symbols. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Usually, a minimum following distance of _____ should be maintained.
questions.explanation: You should keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. In poor conditions, increase this to at least three seconds.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance while turning. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handlebars.

questions.question: A person who is above the legal drinking age with a minimum blood alcohol content (BAC) of ______ is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: In Louisiana, a person under 21 is legally intoxicated at 0.02 percent BAC or higher. A person 21 or older is legally intoxicated at 0.08 percent BAC or higher. Never operate a vehicle while intoxicated—it is illegal and dangerous.
